question: Which among the following is the highest peak of Tamil Nadu?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Doddabetta.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Doddabetta, at 2,637 metres, is the highest peak in Tamil Nadu, situated in the Nilgiri Hills near Ooty (Udhagamandalam). (डोडाबेट्टा — तमिलनाडु की सबसे ऊँची चोटी)

 

• It is part of the Western Ghats and offers a well-known viewpoint and telescope house overlooking the Nilgiri range.

 

• The Nilgiri Hills form the meeting point of the Western and Eastern Ghats in South India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Anamudi (2,695 m), in Kerala's Idukki district, is the highest peak in South India and the entire Western Ghats, but it lies in Kerala, not Tamil Nadu.

 

• Nanda Devi (7,816 m) in Uttarakhand is the second-highest peak in India after Kangchenjunga.

 

NOTE

 

• Mahendragiri (Option 1): A hill (1,647 m) in the Western Ghats in Tirunelveli district, Tamil Nadu, but not its highest point.

 

• Anamudi (Option 2): The highest peak in Kerala and in all of South India, not in Tamil Nadu.

 

• Nanda Devi (Option 3): Located in Uttarakhand's Garhwal Himalayas, unrelated to Tamil Nadu.

question: Which among the following is not a type of solar eclipse?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Penumbral.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A solar eclipse occurs when the Moon passes between the Sun and the Earth, and is classified into three types: Total, Partial, and Annular. (सूर्य ग्रहण के प्रकार)

 

• In a Total solar eclipse, the Moon completely covers the Sun's disc; in a Partial solar eclipse, only a part of the Sun is covered.

 

• In an Annular solar eclipse, the Moon covers the central part of the Sun, leaving a bright ring ("ring of fire") visible around it.

 

• Penumbral is a term used exclusively for lunar eclipses, referring to a lunar eclipse where the Moon passes through the Earth's faint outer shadow (penumbra) only, causing subtle dimming.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Lunar eclipses are classified as Total, Partial, and Penumbral, based on how the Moon passes through Earth's umbra and penumbra.

 

• A solar eclipse can only occur on a New Moon day, while a lunar eclipse can only occur on a Full Moon day.

 

NOTE

 

• Annular (Option 1): A genuine type of solar eclipse producing the 'ring of fire' effect.

 

• Partial (Option 2): A genuine type of solar eclipse where the Moon covers only part of the Sun.

 

• Total (Option 4): A genuine type of solar eclipse where the Moon fully covers the Sun.

question: Shri Bismillah khan was a famous player of musical instrument ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shehnai.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ustad Bismillah Khan (1916–2006) was India's most celebrated shehnai player, credited with bringing the instrument from folk and ceremonial settings to the concert stage. (शहनाई वादक)

 

• He was honoured with the Bharat Ratna in 2001, India's highest civilian award, becoming only the third classical musician to receive it.

 

• He famously performed from the Red Fort on the eve of India's independence on 15 August 1947, and his shehnai recital has since been a Republic Day/Independence Day tradition on All India Radio.

 

• He also received the Bharatiya Gyanpith Award and multiple Padma awards (Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan, Padma Vibhushan).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The shehnai is a wind instrument, similar to the oboe, traditionally associated with auspicious occasions like weddings in North India.

 

• Bismillah Khan hailed from Bihar and was closely associated with Varanasi (Banaras), where he lived and performed for most of his life.

 

NOTE

 

• Tabla (Option 1): A percussion instrument; famous tabla players include Zakir Hussain and Alla Rakha, not Bismillah Khan.

 

• Drum (Option 2): A generic percussion instrument, unrelated to Bismillah Khan's expertise.

 

• Veena (Option 4): A stringed instrument associated with artists like S. Balachander and Chitti Babu, not Bismillah Khan.

question: Who was appointed as the new Director General of National Investigation Agency (NIA) in June 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dinkar Gupta.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dinkar Gupta, a 1987-batch IPS officer and former Director General of Police (DGP), Punjab, was appointed the Director General of the National Investigation Agency (NIA) in June 2022. (राष्ट्रीय जांच एजेंसी के महानिदेशक)

 

• The NIA is India's premier counter-terrorism investigating agency, established after the 26/11 Mumbai attacks under the National Investigation Agency Act, 2008.

 

• The NIA functions under the Ministry of Home Affairs and its headquarters are in New Delhi.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Dinkar Gupta succeeded Kuldiep Singh (who was holding additional charge) as NIA chief.

 

• The NIA has the mandate to investigate offences related to terrorism, human trafficking, counterfeit currency, and other national-security matters across India without needing special state permission.

 

NOTE

 

• Anshul Mishra (Option 2): Not associated with the NIA's leadership in June 2022.

 

• Yashwant Sonawane (Option 3): Not associated with the NIA's leadership in June 2022.

 

• Kiran Bedi (Option 4): A well-known former IPS officer and former Lieutenant Governor of Puducherry, but she had no role in the NIA appointment in June 2022.

question: Which of the following countries is NOT one of the co-hosts of the ICC 2027 ODI World Cup?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kenya.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The ICC Men's ODI Cricket World Cup 2027 is scheduled to be co-hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe, and Namibia, marking cricket's return to the African continent as a World Cup host after 24 years (since the 2003 edition). (क्रिकेट विश्व कप 2027 के सह-मेजबान)

 

• Kenya, though a cricket-playing African nation with ODI history (it co-hosted matches of the 2003 World Cup), is not one of the designated hosts for the 2027 edition.

 

• The tournament is set to run across host venues in these three nations, expanding cricket's footprint in Africa.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 2023 ODI World Cup was hosted solely by India.

 

• South Africa previously co-hosted the 2003 Cricket World Cup along with Zimbabwe and Kenya.

 

NOTE

 

• Zimbabwe (Option 1): A confirmed co-host nation for the 2027 ODI World Cup.

 

• Namibia (Option 3): A confirmed co-host nation for the 2027 ODI World Cup.

 

• South Africa (Option 4): A confirmed co-host nation for the 2027 ODI World Cup, and the lead host.

question: Babur, the first Mughal emperor, succeeded to the throne of Ferghana in ______ when he was 12 years old.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1494.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Babur (Zahir-ud-din Muhammad Babur) succeeded to the throne of the small Central Asian kingdom of Ferghana in 1494, at the age of 12, following the death of his father Umar Sheikh Mirza. (फरगना की गद्दी पर बाबर का राज्यारोहण)

 

• Babur was a descendant of Timur on his father's side and of Genghis Khan on his mother's side.

 

• After being pushed out of Central Asia, Babur turned towards India, defeating Ibrahim Lodi in the First Battle of Panipat in 1526, founding the Mughal Empire.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Babur ruled India until his death in 1530, after which his son Humayun succeeded him.

 

• Babur authored his memoirs, the Baburnama, originally written in Chagatai Turkic.

 

NOTE

 

• 1526 (Option 2): The year Babur won the First Battle of Panipat and founded the Mughal Empire in India, not the year he became ruler of Ferghana.

 

• 1504 (Option 3): The year Babur captured Kabul, establishing his base after losing Samarkand and Ferghana.

 

• 1530 (Option 4): The year of Babur's death, after which Humayun became emperor.

question: Which article of the Indian constitution states that “Governor has power to promulgate ordinances during recess of legislature”?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 213.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 213 of the Indian Constitution grants the Governor the power to promulgate ordinances during the recess of the state legislature, when immediate action is deemed necessary. (राज्यपाल की अध्यादेश जारी करने की शक्ति)

 

• An ordinance issued under Article 213 has the same force and effect as an Act of the state legislature but must be approved by the legislature within six weeks of its reassembly, or it ceases to operate.

 

• This power is analogous to the President's ordinance-making power under Article 123 at the Union level.

 

• The Governor cannot promulgate an ordinance without instructions from the President in certain matters that would have required the President's assent as a Bill.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 213 falls under Part VI of the Constitution, which deals with the states.

 

• Ordinance-making is a legislative power exercised by the executive (Governor/President) only when the legislature is not in session.

 

NOTE

 

• 212 (Option 1): Deals with courts not inquiring into proceedings of the state legislature.

 

• 214 (Option 2): Provides for the establishment of a High Court for each state.

 

• 210 (Option 4): Deals with the language to be used in the state legislature.

question: Which of the following river forms the Dhuadhar falls?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Narmada.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Dhuandhar Falls (meaning “smoke cascade,” as the water spray resembles smoke) is formed by the river Narmada at Bhedaghat, near Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh. (धुआंधार जलप्रपात — नर्मदा नदी)

 

• The falls occur where the Narmada, flowing through the famous Marble Rocks (Bhedaghat) gorge, drops from a height of about 15 metres (around 30 metres by some measures).

 

• The Narmada originates from Amarkantak in Madhya Pradesh and flows westward into the Arabian Sea via the Gulf of Khambhat, making it one of the few major west-flowing rivers of India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Narmada forms the traditional boundary between North and South India.

 

• Other notable Narmada-related falls/sites include the marble rock gorge cruises at Bhedaghat, a major tourist attraction.

 

NOTE

 

• Tapi (Option 1): Another west-flowing river of central India, flowing roughly parallel to and south of the Narmada, unrelated to Dhuandhar Falls.

 

• Godavari (Option 3): The largest peninsular river of India, flowing eastward into the Bay of Bengal, unrelated to Dhuandhar Falls.

 

• Mahanadi (Option 4): A major river of Chhattisgarh and Odisha, unrelated to Dhuandhar Falls.

question: Leo Tolstoy is best known for his ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is novels.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Leo Tolstoy (1828–1910) was a Russian writer widely regarded as one of the greatest novelists of all time. (लियो टॉलस्टॉय — रूसी उपन्यासकार)

 

• His most celebrated novels are War and Peace (1869) and Anna Karenina (1877–78), both landmark works of world literature.

 

• He also wrote The Death of Ivan Ilyich and Resurrection, and his philosophy of non-violent resistance influenced figures like Mahatma Gandhi.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tolstoy corresponded with Gandhi, and Gandhi named his ashram in South Africa “Tolstoy Farm” in his honour.

 

• Tolstoy was born into Russian nobility on his family estate, Yasnaya Polyana.

 

NOTE

 

• dance (Option 1): Not associated with Tolstoy, who was a writer, not a dancer.

 

• acting (Option 2): Not associated with Tolstoy's body of work.

 

• direction (Option 3): Not associated with Tolstoy; he was not a film or theatre director.

question: Which of the following rocks may also contain fossils of plants, animals and other microorganisms that once lived on them?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sedimentary rocks.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sedimentary rocks are formed by the compaction and cementation of sediments (weathered/eroded material, organic matter) deposited in layers, typically in water bodies. (अवसादी चट्टानें — जीवाश्म युक्त)

 

• Because they form through gradual deposition at low temperature and pressure, dead plants, animals, and microorganisms trapped within the layers can be preserved as fossils over time.

 

• Common examples of sedimentary rocks include sandstone, limestone, and shale.

 

• Coal and some limestones are themselves examples of fossil-rich or organically derived sedimentary rocks.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Igneous rocks form from the cooling and solidification of molten magma/lava, and their extreme heat destroys any organic material, so they do not contain fossils.

 

• Metamorphic rocks form under intense heat and pressure, which typically destroys or badly distorts any pre-existing fossils.

 

NOTE

 

• Extrusive igneous rocks (Option 2): Formed when lava cools rapidly on the Earth's surface (e.g., basalt); the intense heat prevents fossil preservation.

 

• Metamorphic rocks (Option 3): Formed by transformation of existing rocks under heat and pressure (e.g., marble, slate); fossils are rarely, if ever, preserved intact.

 

• Intrusive igneous rocks (Option 4): Formed when magma cools slowly beneath the Earth's surface (e.g., granite); no fossils are found in them.

question: Which of the following is a common type of Bryophyta?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Marchantia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Marchantia is a genus of liverworts, one of the most well-known and commonly cited examples of the plant division Bryophyta. (मार्केंशिया — ब्रायोफाइटा का उदाहरण)

 

• Bryophytes are simple, non-vascular land plants (including mosses, liverworts, and hornworts) often called the “amphibians of the plant kingdom” since they need water for reproduction.

 

• Other classic bryophyte examples include Funaria (a moss) and Riccia (a liverwort), alongside Marchantia.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bryophytes lack true roots, stems, and leaves, and instead have root-like rhizoids.

 

• They are considered the first land plants to have evolved from aquatic ancestors (algae).

 

NOTE

 

• Cladophora (Option 1): A genus of green algae, not a bryophyte.

 

• Marsilea (Option 2): A genus of aquatic ferns, belonging to division Pteridophyta, not Bryophyta.

 

• Monocot (Option 4): Refers to monocotyledonous flowering plants (angiosperms), an entirely different and far more advanced plant group.

question: Who among the following Bollywood actress wrote "Unfinished: A Memoir"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Priyanka Chopra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Priyanka Chopra Jonas authored the memoir “Unfinished”, published in 2021, chronicling her personal and professional journey from Bareilly to Bollywood and Hollywood. (प्रियंका चोपड़ा की आत्मकथा)

 

• The book became a New York Times bestseller shortly after its release.

 

• Priyanka Chopra won the Miss World title in 2000 and went on to become a leading actress in Bollywood and later in Hollywood/international television (e.g., Quantico).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Priyanka Chopra is also a UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador and a recipient of the Padma Shri award.

 

• The memoir covers her struggles with self-identity, career setbacks, and her rise as a global icon.

 

NOTE

 

• Kareena Kapoor (Option 2): Authored pregnancy/parenting books such as “Kareena Kapoor Khan's Pregnancy Bible,” not “Unfinished: A Memoir.”

 

• Alia Bhatt (Option 3): Has not authored a memoir titled “Unfinished.”

 

• Deepika Padukone (Option 4): Known for founding The Live Love Laugh Foundation on mental health, but did not write “Unfinished: A Memoir.”

question: Which of the following is a second generation system?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Honeywell 400.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Second-generation computers (roughly 1955–1964) used transistors instead of vacuum tubes, making them smaller, faster, and more reliable. (द्वितीय पीढ़ी के कंप्यूटर)

 

• The Honeywell 400 was a transistor-based mainframe computer released in the early 1960s, making it a classic example of a second-generation computer system.

 

• Other well-known second-generation computers include the IBM 1401 and CDC 1604.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• First-generation computers (e.g., ENIAC) used vacuum tubes; third-generation computers (e.g., IBM 360) used integrated circuits.

 

• Fourth-generation computers use microprocessors, and this is the generation to which most modern PCs, notebooks, and workstations belong.

 

NOTE

 

• IBM notebooks (Option 1): Modern laptop computers belonging to the fourth generation (microprocessor-based), not second generation.

 

• Sun workstations (Option 2): Advanced microprocessor-based computers from the 1980s onward, part of the fourth generation.

 

• Apple II (Option 4): A popular microprocessor-based personal computer released in 1977, belonging to the fourth generation.

question: Which citizen of the Republic of India was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in the year 2014?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kailash Satyarthi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kailash Satyarthi, an Indian children's-rights activist and founder of Bachpan Bachao Andolan, was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2014. (कैलाश सत्यार्थी — नोबेल शांति पुरस्कार 2014)

 

• He shared the prize jointly with Malala Yousafzai of Pakistan, “for their struggle against the suppression of children and young people and for the right of all children to education.”

 

• Satyarthi has led campaigns and rescue operations against child labour and child trafficking in India for decades.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other Indians associated with the Nobel Prize include Rabindranath Tagore (Literature, 1913), C. V. Raman (Physics, 1930), Amartya Sen (Economics, 1998), and Mother Teresa (Peace, 1979).

 

• Satyarthi is the second Indian, after Mother Teresa, to win the Nobel Peace Prize.

 

NOTE

 

• Amartya Sen (Option 1): Won the Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences in 1998, not the Peace Prize.

 

• C. V. Raman (Option 2): Won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1930 for discovering the Raman Effect.

 

• Rabindranath Tagore (Option 4): Won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913 for his work Gitanjali, becoming the first non-European Nobel laureate.

question: Which of the following is NOT a non-contact force?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Friction.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Non-contact forces act between objects without them physically touching each other, such as gravitational, electrostatic (electric), and magnetic forces. (अस्पर्श बल)

 

• Friction, on the other hand, is a contact force — it arises only when two surfaces are in direct physical contact and resist relative motion between them.

 

• Other examples of contact forces include the normal force, tension, and applied (muscular) force.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gravitational force acts between any two masses regardless of distance, as described by Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation.

 

• Electrostatic and magnetic forces act between charged particles and magnets, respectively, without any physical contact.

 

NOTE

 

• Gravitational (Option 1): A non-contact force that acts between any two masses.

 

• Electrostatic (Option 2): A non-contact force that acts between electrically charged bodies.

 

• Magnetic (Option 4): A non-contact force that acts between magnets or magnetic materials.

question: Who was appointed as the new chairman of Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) in June 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nitin Gupta.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Nitin Gupta, an IRS (Income Tax cadre, 1986 batch) officer, took over as Chairman of the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) on 27 June 2022. (केंद्रीय प्रत्यक्ष कर बोर्ड के अध्यक्ष)

 

• The CBDT is a statutory body under the Central Board of Revenue Act, 1963, functioning under the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance.

 

• CBDT provides inputs for policy and planning of direct taxes and administers direct-tax laws through the Income Tax Department.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Nitin Gupta succeeded J. B. Mohapatra as CBDT chairman.

 

• The CBDT is one of two boards under the Department of Revenue, the other being the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC).

 

NOTE

 

• Atulesh Jindal (Option 1): A former CBDT chairman (2016–2017), not appointed in June 2022.

 

• Rani Singh Nair (Option 2): A former CBDT chairperson (2016), not appointed in June 2022.

 

• Sudha Sharma (Option 3): A former CBDT chairperson (2012–2013), not appointed in June 2022.

question: The One Stop Centre Scheme for women is funded by which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nirbhaya Fund.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The One Stop Centre (OSC) Scheme, launched on 1 April 2015 by the Ministry of Women and Child Development, provides integrated support and assistance to women affected by violence, under one roof. (निर्भया कोष से वित्त पोषित)

 

• The scheme is popularly known as Sakhi and is funded through the Nirbhaya Fund, a corpus set up by the Government of India in 2013 to support initiatives for women's safety and security.

 

• OSCs provide medical aid, police assistance, legal aid, psychological counselling, and temporary shelter to women in distress.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Nirbhaya Fund was created in the aftermath of the December 2012 Delhi gang-rape case to fund projects for enhancing women's safety.

 

• Other schemes funded through the Nirbhaya Fund include Women Helpline (181), Emergency Response Support System (112), and Mahila Police Volunteers.

 

NOTE

 

• Cash Suvidha (Option 1): Not a real government fund associated with the One Stop Centre Scheme.

 

• Saha Fund (Option 2): Not a real government fund associated with the One Stop Centre Scheme.

 

• Rug Beneath My Feet (Option 4): Not a government fund; this is a distractor with no connection to the scheme.

question: Which Indian athlete won first silver medal in weightlifting at Tokyo Olympics 2020 held in 2021?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mirabai Chanu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Saikhom Mirabai Chanu won the silver medal in the women's 49 kg weightlifting category at the Tokyo Olympics 2020 (held in 2021), lifting a total of 202 kg (87 kg snatch + 115 kg clean and jerk). (टोक्यो ओलंपिक — भारोत्तोलन रजत पदक)

 

• This was India's first medal of the Tokyo Olympics 2020 and India's first-ever Olympic medal in weightlifting since 2000 (Karnam Malleswari at Sydney 2000).

 

• She later went on to win a gold medal at the 2022 Commonwealth Games in Birmingham.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Karnam Malleswari was the first Indian woman to win an Olympic medal (bronze, weightlifting, Sydney 2000).

 

• India's overall medal tally at Tokyo 2020 was seven medals — one gold (Neeraj Chopra, javelin), two silver, and four bronze.

 

NOTE

 

• PV Sindhu (Option 1): Won a bronze medal in badminton at Tokyo 2020, not weightlifting.

 

• Neeraj Chopra (Option 2): Won India's only gold medal, in javelin throw, at Tokyo 2020, not weightlifting.

 

• Ravi Dahiya (Option 3): Won a silver medal in wrestling (57 kg freestyle) at Tokyo 2020, not weightlifting.

question: In India, the electoral bonds are valid for how many days from the date of issue?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fifteen days.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Electoral Bonds, introduced via the Electoral Bond Scheme, 2018, are financial instruments (like promissory notes) issued by the State Bank of India (SBI) for making anonymous donations to political parties. (चुनावी बॉन्ड की वैधता — 15 दिन)

 

• An electoral bond is valid for fifteen calendar days from the date of issue, within which it must be encashed by the eligible political party through its verified bank account.

 

• If the bond is not encashed within 15 days, the amount is deposited by the bank into the Prime Minister's National Relief Fund.

 

• Only political parties registered under the Representation of the People Act, 1951, and having secured at least 1% of votes in the last Lok Sabha/Assembly election, are eligible to receive electoral bonds.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Electoral bonds are issued in multiples of Rs. 1,000, Rs. 10,000, Rs. 1 lakh, Rs. 10 lakh, and Rs. 1 crore.

 

• The Supreme Court of India struck down the Electoral Bond Scheme as unconstitutional in February 2024, well after this exam's reference period.

 

NOTE

 

• Thirty days (Option 2): Not the actual validity period; incorrect.

 

• Seven days (Option 3): Not the actual validity period; incorrect.

 

• Fourteen days (Option 4): Close to but not the correct figure; the scheme specifies fifteen days, not fourteen.

question:
In the given expression of GDP according to the expenditure method, which of the following represents the aggregate imports expenditure incurred by the economy?
C + I + G + X – M
solution_text:
The correct answer is M.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under the expenditure method of calculating GDP, the formula is: GDP = C + I + G + (X – M). (व्यय विधि द्वारा जीडीपी गणना)

 

• Here, C stands for private final consumption expenditure, I for gross investment (capital formation), G for government expenditure, X for exports, and M for imports.

 

• Imports (M) are subtracted because they represent expenditure on goods and services produced outside the domestic economy and must not be counted as part of domestic output.

 

• Exports (X), in contrast, are added because they represent domestically produced goods and services sold abroad.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The term (X – M) in the formula represents Net Exports.

 

• The expenditure method is one of the three standard approaches to estimating GDP, the other two being the income method and the production (value-added) method.

 

NOTE

 

• C (Option 1): Represents private final consumption expenditure, not imports.

 

• I (Option 3): Represents gross investment/capital formation, not imports.

 

• X (Option 4): Represents exports, not imports.

question: Zakir Hussain is associated with which musical Instrument?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tabla.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ustad Zakir Hussain is one of India's most celebrated tabla players, son of the legendary tabla maestro Ustad Alla Rakha. (उस्ताद जाकिर हुसैन — तबला वादक)

 

• He has collaborated extensively in Indian classical, fusion, and world music, notably as part of the group Shakti with guitarist John McLaughlin.

 

• He is a recipient of the Padma Shri (1988), Padma Bhushan (2002), Padma Vibhushan (2023), and multiple Grammy Awards.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Zakir Hussain won three Grammy Awards in a single ceremony in 2024, a first for an Indian musician.

 

• The tabla is a pair of hand drums central to Hindustani classical music.

 

NOTE

 

• Violin (Option 1): Associated with artists like L. Subramaniam and M. S. Gopalakrishnan, not Zakir Hussain.

 

• Guitar (Option 2): Not Zakir Hussain's instrument, though he has performed with guitarists like John McLaughlin.

 

• Shehnai (Option 4): Associated with Ustad Bismillah Khan, not Zakir Hussain.

question: ______ administration became the model followed by the great emperor Akbar when he consolidated the Mughal Empire.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sher Shah Suri’s.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sher Shah Suri, the founder of the Suri dynasty who briefly displaced the Mughals (1540–1545), introduced significant administrative and revenue reforms, including a well-organised system of land revenue assessment (zabt system), roads (Grand Trunk Road), and currency reform (the rupiya). (शेरशाह सूरी का प्रशासनिक मॉडल)

 

• When Akbar consolidated and expanded the Mughal Empire, he adopted and further refined Sher Shah Suri's administrative model, especially in matters of land revenue administration, which was later developed further by his finance minister Raja Todar Mal.

 

• Sher Shah's administration divided the empire into Sarkars and Parganas, a structure that influenced Mughal provincial administration.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sher Shah Suri defeated Humayun (Akbar's father) and ruled North India from 1540 to 1545.

 

• Akbar's revenue system, the Dahsala system, built upon principles first introduced under Sher Shah's regime.

 

NOTE

 

• Alauddin Khalji’s (Option 2): A Delhi Sultanate ruler known for market-control reforms and Mongol-defence measures, not the model Akbar followed.

 

• Muhammad Tughluq’s (Option 3): Known for controversial measures like the transfer of capital to Daulatabad and token currency, not the model followed by Akbar.

 

• Genghis Khan’s (Option 4): The Mongol conqueror, unrelated to Mughal administrative structure; in fact, Mughals descended from him but did not model administration on his system.

question: Which Indian player won the most medals at Commonwealth games 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sharath Kamal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Achanta Sharath Kamal, India's veteran table tennis player, won four medals (three gold and one silver) at the 2022 Commonwealth Games in Birmingham, the most medals by any Indian athlete at that edition. (शरत कमल — सर्वाधिक पदक)

 

• His medals came in men's singles (gold), men's team event (gold), mixed doubles (gold, with Sreeja Akula), and men's doubles (silver, with Sathiyan Gnanasekaran).

 

• He was also India's flag-bearer at the closing ceremony of CWG 2022.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India finished CWG 2022 with a total of 61 medals (22 gold, 16 silver, 23 bronze), ranking fourth overall.

 

• Sharath Kamal became the oldest Indian to win a CWG gold medal in table tennis singles at the time.

 

NOTE

 

• Pusarla Venkata Sindhu (Option 1): Won a gold medal in women's singles badminton at CWG 2022, but only one medal, not the most.

 

• Amit Panghal (Option 2): Won a silver medal in boxing at CWG 2022, but only one medal.

 

• Sathiyan Gnanasekaran (Option 4): Won medals in table tennis including men's doubles silver (with Sharath Kamal) and team gold, but fewer overall than Sharath Kamal.

question: The world’s highest motorable road passes through ______ pass in India, as of 2022.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Umling La.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Umling La Pass, located in Ladakh at an altitude of about 19,024 feet (5,798 metres), was developed by the Border Roads Organisation (BRO) and opened in 2021. (उमलिंग ला दर्रा — दुनिया की सबसे ऊंची सड़क)

 

• It is recognised as the world's highest motorable road, surpassing the previous record held by roads in the region.

 

• The pass connects Chisumle and Demchok villages in eastern Ladakh, close to the Line of Actual Control (LAC).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The road was built as part of BRO's Project Himank.

 

• Umling La surpassed the earlier claimant, the Semo La pass, and roads in Bolivia/Chile that had previously been cited for high-altitude motorable claims.

 

NOTE

 

• Khunjerab (Option 1): A high mountain pass (about 4,693 m) on the China–Pakistan border, connecting Xinjiang and Gilgit-Baltistan, not in India and not the world's highest.

 

• Rohtang (Option 2): A mountain pass (about 3,978 m) in Himachal Pradesh connecting the Kullu Valley to Lahaul-Spiti, much lower than Umling La.

 

• Dihang (Option 3): Associated with the Dihang river/gorge in Arunachal Pradesh, not a record-holding high-altitude motorable pass.

question: Which of the following is NOT a valid file format in MS-Word 365?
solution_text:
The correct answer is .dcp.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• MS-Word supports several valid file formats for documents and templates, including .doc (older binary document format), .docx (modern XML-based document format, default since Word 2007), and .dotx (XML-based template format). (माइक्रोसॉफ्ट वर्ड फ़ाइल प्रारूप)

 

• .dcp is not a recognised Microsoft Word file format; it is not among the extensions used for saving Word documents or templates.

 

• Other valid Word-related formats include .docm (macro-enabled document) and .dotm (macro-enabled template).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The .docx format, introduced with Office 2007, is based on the Office Open XML (OOXML) standard and is more compact and robust than the older binary .doc format.

 

• MS-Word can also save/export to other general formats like .pdf, .rtf, and .txt.

 

NOTE

 

• .dotx (Option 1): A valid Word template file format (XML-based).

 

• .doc (Option 3): A valid, older binary Word document format (pre-2007).

 

• .docx (Option 4): The valid, current default Word document format (XML-based, post-2007).
